subject: SLA exception request: external moderation & structured-output validation (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Tara Hu <tara.hu@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: carve-out for moderation + structured-output validations

Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re spinning Redwood into a customer-facing triage flow where a small percentage of requests (mostly clinical notes) pass through a third‑party content moderation vendor and a structured-output validator before downstream systems. During peak hours the vendor validation adds 250–600ms on top of Redwood’s median latency reported in the benchmark PDF.

This is creating a mismatch with our contract target (99.95% sub-300ms median for the critical route). Procurement asked whether Redwood can grant a targeted SLA carve-out/exclusion for the time spent in third‑party moderation and structured-output validation, or alternatively provide documented fallback behavior and credits when the vendor validation adds >200ms.

I attached a short request packet (acme_sla_carveout_request_20270218.pdf) and a sample incident log (moderation-incident-log-20270217.csv). Can you loop in the right people and let us know if an interim carve-out + mitigations is possible while we harden the integration?

—Tara
Tara Hu
Senior Product Manager, Acme Health
attachments: acme_sla_carveout_request_20270218.pdf, moderation-incident-log-20270217.csv

Forwarding Acme’s carve-out packet — short ask below. TL;DR: they want either (A) a limited SLA exclusion for the vendor/validator latency window or (B) clear fallback rules + credits when vendor validation adds >200ms. They’re asking for something interim while their integration stabilizes.

Proposed immediate steps:
- Engineering: confirm whether we can attribute vendor/validator time in our latency breakdowns and expose that in token-level traces.
- Product: define a mitigation matrix (fallback model variant, circuit breaker thresholds, cached responses).
- Legal: propose conditional carve-out language and approval matrix for procurement.

Can you review and I’ll coordinate with Acme on timelines. Added Tara and procurement to keep everyone in the loop.

Thanks —
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments referenced: acme_sla_carveout_request_20270218.pdf

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-19T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: carve-out for moderation + structured-output validations

Ben / team —

Quick technical readout after reviewing the incident log. We can surface vendor validation latency separately in our traces if the vendor adds a custom header or we proxy through our validation shim. Options:

1) Attribution-only: mark vendor/validator time as an "external validation" bucket in per-request traces. This requires a small shim and a flag from the integration (ETA: 2–3 days dev + 1 day QA). No SLA change required, but gives procurement the data they want.

2) Runtime fallback: when validator latency exceeds X ms (configurable), route to a cached/quantized model variant that avoids the validator call. This would reduce end-to-end median, but changes output quality; needs customer opt-in. Engineering ETA: 2 weeks for safe rollout + canary.

3) Credit automation: if vendor validation >200ms, automatically flag the request and produce a credit event for reconciliation. Implementation depends on whether Acme wants token-level or route-level credits.

I attached a short mitigation draft (draft-carveout-mitigation-plan.pdf) with recommended thresholds. I flagged three risk cases: stateful transactions where structured-output validation prevents downstream corruption; PII-heavy payloads where skipping validation is not acceptable; and vendor unavailability windows.

Questions for legal/sales: what conditional language do we need to protect against repeated vendor-induced outages?

—Aditya
Director, Product, Redwood Inference
attachments: draft-carveout-mitigation-plan.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-20T09:55:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: carve-out for moderation + structured-output validations

On Thu, Feb 18, 2027 at 9:12 AM Tara Hu <tara.hu@acmehealth.com> wrote:
> Ben —
>
> Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re spinning Redwood into a customer-facing triage flow where a small percentage of requests (mostly clinical notes) pass through a third‑party content moderation vendor and a structured-output validator before downstream systems. During peak hours the vendor validation adds 250–600ms on top of Redwood’s median latency reported in the benchmark PDF.

Folks — my read from infra: we can do two safe paths that preserve reliability while minimizing SLA exposure:

- Opt A (short-term carve-out): Scope an explicit exclusion for "external validation window" where latency incurred by a named third-party vendor (Acme-specified) does not count toward Redwood's latency SLO for the specific route. Conditions: vendor must be declared in the contract, per-request attribution must be visible in logs, and Redwood must maintain a fallback behavior (cached/quantized variant) for >95th percentile vendor delays. Operationally: we’ll add a per-route flag and an alert runbook.

- Opt B (no carve-out, fallback-only): No SLA change; instead we guarantee automatic fallback and a credit policy when vendor time exceeds threshold. This shifts more work to billing reconciliation.

Risks and mitigations:
- Data safety: if structured-output validation is skipped, we risk downstream corruption for stateful workflows. Mitigation: carve-out allowed only for stateless read-only routes or routes with customer opt-in after signoff.
- Regressions: require a 2-week canary on dedicated traffic and a short QA checklist.

I’ve sketched a proposed approval matrix in the attached draft and included the incident log notes. If legal can draft the conditional carve-out clause (narrowly scoped, time-bound, vendor-named), I can own the rollout runbook and monitoring.

—Marissa
Principal Engineer, Runtime Reliability, Redwood Inference
attachments: moderation-incident-log-20270217.csv

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tara Hu <tara.hu@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-02-21T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: carve-out for moderation + structured-output validations

Tara / Acme / team —

Thank you for the clear packet. After reviewing the technical notes and the proposed mitigations, legal can provisionally approve a narrowly scoped SLA exclusion for the named external validator under these conditions: 

1) Scope & duration: exclusion applies only to route "acme/clinical-triage" for a six‑month pilot window (start date to be negotiated).
2) Attribution: Redwood will surface a per-request "external_validation_ms" field in traces and in the route latency breakdown exported to Acme.
3) Fallback & safety: Redwood will enable the fallback model variant when external_validation_ms > 200ms; fallback behavior will be explicitly documented and require Acme opt-in for stateful routes.
4) Credits & monitoring: if external_validation_ms > 500ms for >0.5% of daily requests for 3 consecutive days, Redwood will issue a credit equal to X (TBD) and open an incident review.
5) Vendor naming: the carve-out must list the vendor(s) by legal entity and be revocable if vendor fails to meet agreed controls.

Next steps — Ben, can you (1) confirm Acme is comfortable with the pilot scope and opt-in constraints, (2) run procurement through the DocuSign with the draft carve-out clause, and (3) coordinate scheduling for a 2‑week canary? I’ve attached a one‑page approval matrix (draft-carveout-mitigation-plan.pdf) with conditional language we can drop into the SOW.

If procurement agrees, Legal will sign the pilot SOW and we’ll move to scheduling.

Regards —
Lauren Bishop
Head of Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference
attachments: draft-carveout-mitigation-plan.pdf, acme_sla_carveout_request_20270218.pdf
